title: Surgelet reconciler: Admin API bridge for runbooks-as-actions
creator: Aisha Kapur
description: Build a lightweight reconciler ("Surgelet") that exposes an admin-facing API to convert authored runbook fragments into discrete, idempotent actions that can be queued and executed by the operator platform. The reconciler is intended to: 1) provide a canonical mapping from runbook steps to atomic admin API calls, 2) surface dry-run and validation errors early, 3) emit structured telemetry for cost/latency breakdowns, and 4) enforce RBAC + audit logging for any ephemeral admin actions. This ticket covers the core API, the reconciler engine, and a minimal integration shim for the runbook editor to push fragments as tasks.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /surgelet/convert accepts a runbook fragment (yaml/json) and returns a normalized action graph + validation report
Idempotency: Every generated action includes an idempotency key and deterministic fingerprint that prevents duplicate side-effects on retries
Dry-run: The reconciler supports a dry_run=true mode that validates preconditions without mutating any infra and returns a simulated execution trace
RBAC: Requests are validated against RBAC rules and audit metadata is written to customer audit-log sink; tests cover admin roles and forbidden scenarios
Telemetry: Each conversion emits a trace with timing, tokenization counts, rule hits, and estimated token cost stored in the ops metrics dashboard
Integration: Runbook editor can push a fragment and receive a task id; the task is visible in the admin task queue UI and can be simulated/executed
Tests: End-to-end test verifies conversion -> queue -> simulated-execute path and asserts no side effects during dry-run
design_notes: Prefer a small, language-agnostic payload format (canonical JSON) so the reconciler can be used by Console, CLI and third-party integrators
Use deterministic hashing of step content + environment fingerprint to generate idempotency keys (SHA256 + namespace) rather than timestamp-based IDs
Keep the reconciler stateless: store only transient conversion artifacts in a fast TTL store and persist canonical action manifests to the existing operator task store on finalize
Leverage existing RBAC library from identity-service to avoid introducing new permission semantics
Trade-offs: strict validation increases developer UX but may block exploratory edits; we provide a permissive 'operator-preview' flag to bypass hard validation in non-production clusters
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch and unit tests (2 days)
2) Internal alpha: deploy to ops-dev with dry-run enforced, enable telemetry and smoke integration tests (3 days)
3) Canary: allow limited manual execute for SRE team in ops-staging, monitor metrics and error budget impact (5 days)
4) Gradual enablement: by team opt-in with canary TTL of 48h, collect feedback and fix issues
5) GA: flip default to enabled for all internal admin clusters after 2 weeks of stable canary
risks_mitigation: Risk: accidental destructive execution from malformed fragments -> Mitigation: default to dry-run and require explicit finalization endpoint with two-step commit
Risk: permission escalation via reconciler payload -> Mitigation: validate every action against RBAC and deny any action that would grant new privileges
Risk: noisy telemetry or cost spikes -> Mitigation: capped conversion rate per-tenant and token-cost estimate alarms wired to paging
Risk: incompatibility with existing task runner -> Mitigation: adapter layer that emits both legacy and new manifest shapes for 2 release cycles
